title: Sprint bridge: latency & cost communique
content:
Purpose: weekly bridge note capturing the observability sprint sync where tracing sampling experiments, dashboard ownership handoffs, and cost-telemetry heuristics were discussed. This is a working comms doc intended for engineers and platform PMs; please add inline comments or update the linked artifacts if you own an item.

Attendees:
- Ravi Menon (owner)
- Ellie Chen
- Marco Alvarez
- Priya Kapoor
- Jordan Lee
- Guests: Nidhi Rao (billing), Aaron Park (platform infra)

Quick summary / headline decisions:
1) Approve limited adaptive-head sampling pilot for high-throughput endpoints (payments, chat-ingest). Pilot parameters: head-sample-rate=1.0 for errors, default head-sample-rate=0.02 for success traces, tail-sample multiplier up to 3x for traces > 200 spans.
   - Purpose: cut span ingestion by ~55% on noisy endpoints while preserving error/failure visibility.
   - Rollout: EU region starting 2026-11-09 (canary), then US on 2026-11-12 if canary metrics look good.
2) Dashboard ownership reassignments: Ellie to own 'Span Economics' dashboard, Marco to own 'Per-route token cost' and 'KV-cache hit rate' charts.
3) Cost alerts: new burn-rate alert for span-invoice projection (threshold initial = 120% of forecast) -> triggers paging and activates temporary reduced-sampling policy.
4) Backfill policy: keep 30 days of high-fidelity traces, mark prior to 30 days as sampled/aggregated in metrics pipeline to reduce retention costs.

Standup-style updates (short, by person):
- Ravi: drafted canary plan and rollout runbook; blocked on billing export schema change from Nidhi (INF-5121). Action: follow up by 2026-11-05.
- Ellie: initial Span Economics dashboard 80% complete; added per-model and per-region tabs; needs sample data from US canary. Action: complete by 2026-11-07.
- Marco: prototyped per-route token cost chart using token_count tags; synthetic dataset shows 18% variance vs actual spend — tracking down mapping mismatch (likely service-proxy tag loss). Filed JIRA-OBS-4312.
- Priya: implemented early-stage adaptive sampler in staging, integrated metrics exporter for sampler decisions (sampled_count, drop_count, head_hits). Needs infra quota bump for extra staging ingestion. Action: request quota from Aaron.
- Jordan: dashboard access audit done; removed stale editors; started draft of dashboard runbook (title: how-to-on-call).

Data and telemetry notes:
- Baselines: current monthly span ingestion ~1.2B spans. Pilot target is to reduce by ~600M spans for noisy endpoints.
- Sampling metrics we'll watch during canary: errors-per-million, sampled_error_recall, tail-span retention ratio, median latency of trace ingestion pipeline.
- Billing: Nidhi provided latest invoice projections — notable line-item growth in "trace-storage-append" due to long tails from cache-warmups in backend. Investigate aggregating warmup-only spans.

Runbook & fallback behavior (agreed):
- Canary window 48 hours with active monitoring. Success criteria: no >10% increase in mean error-rate for canary endpoints, no >5% drop in sampled_error_recall.
- If invoice burn-rate alert trips (>=150% of forecast within 7 days), automation will apply temporary sampling-reduction policy (global default head-sample-rate -> 0.01) and notify oncall.
- On escalations, fallback to 'full-trace-on-error' policy (guarantee: any trace tagged with error=true must be sampled at head-sample-rate=1.0).

Dashboard work items (owners + due dates):
- Span Economics (Ellie) — add cost-per-1M-span panel, annotate last 3 deploys. Due 2026-11-07.
- Per-route token cost (Marco) — validate mapping and fix lost tags. Due 2026-11-09.
- Ingestion pipeline latency dashboard (Ravi/Jordan) — add histogram view for ingestion queue times. Due 2026-11-08.

Experiments and metrics to collect in canary:
- sampled_error_recall (goal >95%)
- span_inflow_rate (goal drop >=40% on targeted endpoints)
- ingestion_latency_p95 (goal <= baseline + 10ms)
- estimated_monthly_savings (projection metric; update live after 24h of canary)

Open questions & blockers:
- Billing export schema change (INF-5121) must land before accurate cost dashboards for the US canary. Nidhi to confirm ETA.
- Quota: staging ingestion needs temporary bump; Aaron to scope cost and grant by 2026-11-06.
- Compliance: confirm aggregated-span retention meets PII guidelines for EU customers — Priya to loop in Legal.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: adaptive sampling hides low-frequency but high-impact regressions. Mitigation: keep error-based sampling at 100% and attach synthetic-probe traces weekly for regression checks.
- Risk: dashboard owners overloaded in sprint. Mitigation: slice dashboards into MVP (owner) + nice-to-have (shared).

Action items (concise):
- Ravi: follow up with Nidhi on INF-5121 (due 2026-11-05).
- Ellie: finish Span Economics dashboard (due 2026-11-07).
- Marco: resolve tag loss mapping (JIRA-OBS-4312) and re-run cost model (due 2026-11-09).
- Priya: request staging quota and validate sampler telemetry (due 2026-11-06).
- Jordan: finalize oncall dashboard runbook (due 2026-11-08).

Next check-in: asynchronous updates to this doc; formal post-canary review meeting scheduled 2026-11-14 10:00 PT (30m) to decide wider rollout.

Notes & references added during sync:
- Temporary policy snippet (sampler): head_rate=0.02, error_head_rate=1.0, tail_multiplier=3.
- Quick link: Confluence page (linked_artifacts) contains full experiment design and telemetry dashboards.

Small freeform notes (from chat during meeting):
- "If we can shave off the warmup spans we might get 8-12% further savings without touching core sampling" — Marco
- "We should keep a daily synthetic trace that simulates a 500-span long-runner to catch tail regressions" — Priya

If you are assigned an action, please update the linked JIRA or add a short note below this doc with status. This file is intentionally concise; we will expand the post-canary report with charts and raw numbers in the Confluence experiment page.

Document history:
- 2026-11-04: Created (Ravi)
- 2026-11-05: Minor edits: clarified canary dates, added Jira refs (Ravi)
